subject: Possible bug: lr.beta coefficients seem to be fixed to zero

messages.author: f4d0d3b4f14636b6
messages.subject: Possible bug: lr.beta coefficients seem to be fixed to zero
parts:
Hi, 

I'm trying to run a simulated example of a two-factor, latent regression model. It appears that the latent regression coefficients fixed to zero. Below is my full code; in brief, I entered the statement "mod2 <- mirt(dataset, model.2 ,covdata = covdataset, formula = ~-1+x)" and find that "coef(mod2)$lr.betas" results in estimates that exactly equal 0 across all repeated samples (it is equal to 1 in the population).

# Item loadings to generate simulated data
Q_df = data.frame(mat.or.vec(nr = 8, nc = 2))
names(Q_df) = c("F1","F2")
row.names(Q_df) = paste("Item_",1:8, sep = "")
Q_df$F1[1:4] = 1; Q_df$F2[4:8] = 1;

> # Covariance matrix for simulated data
> SQ_df = data.frame(matrix(rep(TRUE,4), nr = 2))
> names(SQ_df) <- row.names(SQ_df) <- names(Q_df)
> 
> Q_df
       F1 F2
Item_1  1  0
Item_2  1  0
Item_3  1  0
Item_4  1  1
Item_5  0  1
Item_6  0  1
Item_7  0  1
Item_8  0  1

> SQ_df
     F1   F2
F1 TRUE TRUE
F2 TRUE TRUE

> model.2 = mirt.model(input = as.matrix(Q_df), COV = as.matrix(SQ_df))
> 
> ### simulate a new matrix
> x = rnorm(2000, 0, 1)
> Theta = cbind(x,x)+mvrnorm(2000, c(0,0),matrix(c(1,0.5,0.5,1), nrow = 2))

> a
     [,1] [,2]
[1,]  1.5   NA
[2,]  0.5   NA
[3,]  1.0   NA
[4,]  1.0  0.5
[5,]   NA  1.5
[6,]   NA  0.5
[7,]   NA  1.0
[8,]   NA  1.0

> d
     [,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,] -1.0   NA   NA
[2,] -1.5   NA   NA
[3,]  1.5   NA   NA
[4,]  0.0   NA   NA
[5,]  3.0    2 -0.5
[6,]  2.5    1 -1.0
[7,]  2.0    0   NA
[8,]  1.0   NA   NA

> items
[1] "dich"   "dich"   "dich"   "dich"   "graded" "graded" "graded" "dich"  

> dataset = simdata(a,d,2000,items,Theta = Theta)

> head(dataset)

     Item_1 Item_2 Item_3 Item_4 Item_5 Item_6 Item_7 Item_8
[1,]      0      0      0      0      0      2      1      0
[2,]      1      0      1      0      2      3      2      0
[3,]      1      0      1      1      2      3      2      1
[4,]      0      0      1      0      2      1      0      1
[5,]      0      0      0      0      2      2      0      1
[6,]      0      0      0      0      2      1      1      1
> #dataset = transform(dataset, x = x)

> covdataset = data.frame(x = x)

> mod2 <- mirt(dataset, model.2 ,covdata = covdataset, formula = ~-1+x)
Iteration: 63, Log-Lik: -12033.454, Max-Change: 0.00009

> coef(mod2)$lr.betas
  F1 F2
x  0  0

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Possible bug: lr.beta coefficients seem to be fixed to zero
parts:
It's hard to tell exactly what's going on here (the syntax wasn't completely reproducible). Why do you have a -1 in the formula interface though? The intercept is automatically removed in these models because otherwise it is not identified. So there's no need to remove it explicitly. 

Phil

parts:
Hi Phil, 

Thanks for the reply. I was trying to be explicit in removing the intercept for identification purposes (hence, the -1 in the formula interface). Removing the -1 fixed the problem. Thanks for your help!

> mod2 <- mirt(dataset, model.2 ,covdata = covdataset, formula = ~x, TOL = 1E-3)
Iteration: 32, Log-Lik: -11438.853, Max-Change: 0.00100

> coef(mod2)$lr.betas
               F1    F2
(Intercept) 0.000 0.000
x           0.919 1.056
